name: cog-rail
title: Cog Rail
description: File/nav tree whose per-depth indent guides are a rack rail and whose keyboard focus is a small mechanical carriage — a foreground square with two tooth notches — that springs along the rail between rows and hops columns on ArrowLeft/Right.
useWhen: Pick cog-rail when the tree is deep enough that people lose track of their vertical position — the payoff is the focus carriage itself, a physical marker that springs row-to-row and hops depth columns on arrow keys, so 'where am I' is answered by a moving object rather than a color change. Pick taproot-trace instead when the more interesting story is the structure drawing itself in as you explore it (an organic root system that grows from each parent's junction on expand) rather than a vehicle tracking your cursor's position through a static rail grid.
instruction: Build a file/nav/org tree where the indentation guides are per-depth straight SVG rails (one 1px --border stroke per depth column, running behind that column's rows) and keyboard focus is rendered as a small mechanical carriage — an inline SVG rounded square in --foreground with two tooth-notch cutouts (small --background rectangles bitten out of its left and right edges) — that physically travels those rails as focus moves. Data is a plain recursive `{ id, label, children? }` tree passed as `nodes`; expand state is uncontrolled (`defaultExpandedIds`), selection and roving-tabindex focus are internal. The carriage's position is derived analytically, never measured: given a fixed row height and a fixed per-depth indent step, the currently focused row's index in the flattened *visible* list gives its y, and its depth gives its x (the same x each row's own rail column already sits on), so the carriage can never drift out of sync with the list ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right are actually walking. It moves via a single CSS transform with an overshoot spring easing (`cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`, ~260ms) — ArrowUp/Down springs it straight along the current rail to the adjacent row, ArrowLeft/Right (which per the ARIA tree pattern below either opens/dives into a child or closes/climbs to a parent) hops it sideways to the new depth's column the instant focus lands there. Expanding a node reveals its children immediately in the DOM (so they are focusable the frame they exist, regardless of animation) but the rail for that block draws downward via the pathLength=1/strokeDasharray=1/strokeDashoffset 0-or-1 trick over ~200ms ease-out-expo, while the children themselves stagger a fade-in + 4px slide at a flat 20ms per row so a newly revealed subtree visibly reads as freshly attached to its parent rather than simply appearing. Collapsing a node is deliberately instantaneous with no leave animation — that is what keeps the analytic row-index math the carriage depends on always exactly in sync with the DOM, with no still-fading subtree changing the effective layout out from under it. Full WAI-ARIA tree pattern: role=tree with an aria-label, role=treeitem rows with aria-expanded (only when the node has children), aria-selected, aria-level, and role=group wrapping each children block; there is no nested <button> or <a> in a row — the disclosure chevron is a decorative aria-hidden mark and a leaf gets a small dot bullet instead, and the treeitem itself is the whole interactive surface (click or Enter/Space selects and, for a folder, toggles). Keyboard model: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move focus over the flattened visible order; ArrowRight opens a closed node without moving focus, or dives to its first child if already open; ArrowLeft closes an open node in place, or climbs to the parent if already closed or a leaf; Home/End jump to the first/last visible row; type-ahead buffers printable characters for 600ms and jumps focus to the next row (wrapping) whose label starts with the buffer. Roving tabindex: exactly one row is ever tab-stoppable, moved imperatively alongside focus on every keyboard or pointer interaction. Rail stroke is --border at rest; the one rail whose direct children include the currently focused row switches to --muted, so the column you're inside of reads differently as you arrow through the tree. The carriage itself is aria-hidden and pointer-events:none — it is a pure visual mirror of the real roving-tabindex DOM focus, so screen readers announce rows natively whether or not the carriage has finished springing to them. Zero dependencies, DOM+SVG+CSS only, no canvas, every color a token (--background --foreground --muted --border --accent). prefers-reduced-motion (read live via matchMedia, not just CSS) makes the carriage teleport instead of spring and every open rail render at full length immediately with no draw-in or stagger, fully usable without any of the motion. Differs from taproot-trace (an organic root system of per-parent branching paths that is the whole point of that component) in both geometry and novelty: here the rails are a plain straight-line grid and the interesting mechanism is the carriage — a distinct physical object with its own easing — traveling them, not the guides drawing themselves.
